chapter: Chicago, the Woodside, the army and 52nd Street
title: Kelly's Stables with Roy and singer Billy Daniels
summary: Ken Corsey played piano at the Arcadia; at Kelly's Stables Billy Daniels arrived from the Black Cat, bringing his crowd.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: I can't think of the whole band. I've been in so many bands in my -- these were just outstanding men. I remember we had a piano player by the name of Ken Corsey, who also doubled on trumpet. I think he did quite a bit of work for Norman Granz at one time, also. But I worked there with him for awhile, and then Roy formed Stables another small band and we went to work in Kelly's Tables, and I worked there with everybody. With Billy Daniels. He was the darling of the lady's man -- oh, what a singer. He could just charm everybody, a tremendous singer, you know.

He had been working previous to that at a club downtown called the Black Cat, and he left and came up to Kelley's Stables and he brought all of his trade with him. Because he was a tremendous entertainer. But I -- he really got big later, he got very big later. But at that time he
was just a club entertainer. But a marvelous singer. I liked his singing better then than I do now.
